symptom: With Studio Pro's <project>.mpr.lock present, `marketplace update` started, printed ~387 'refusing to write … Studio Pro has this project open' warnings, and ended with 'The project may be mid-update — … Restore from version control', exit 1, although nothing had changed.
file: cmd/mxcli/marketplace/update.go PerformUpdate; cmd/mxcli/cmd_marketplace_update.go runMarketplaceUpdate; modelsdk/mpr/studiopro_lock.go CheckStudioProOpen. Test: cmd/mxcli/marketplace/update_studiopro_open_2366_test.go
cause: The Studio Pro guard runs per write (guardWrite), so a multi-unit run met it at the first drop and every write after it; the failure was not marked ErrUpdateNotStarted, so the caller printed its 'mid-update' text.
insight: **A per-write guard needs a per-run check for runs that cannot stop cleanly.** The guard is right for exec (one write, one refusal); a marketplace update is a drop followed by a transplant, so the same guard turns into hundreds of refusals and a false 'restore from version control'. Ask once before the run, mark the error 'not started', and do it before the expensive reference builds.
